 Great Britain has been at the forefront of decarbonising its electricity system, one of the first countries to commit to net zero in law, and a world leader in offshore wind. GB's electricity system is changing quickly, and the planning decisions made today will shape how well it performs in the future. We are seeking a researcher to work within the publicly-funded NextNet project to develop new methods for planning the GB transmission network under uncertainty, working closely with the project's advisors and industry so that the research has a clear route into practice.

 Demand, generation, weather and market conditions are all uncertain, and the way they interact makes network planning increasingly difficult. The post holder will study and classify these sources of uncertainty across both short-term operation and long-term planning and examine how they are connected in space and time, drawing on statistical and probabilistic methods to understand and represent these relationships. This work will feed into a flexible framework for generating realistic, hour by hour scenarios of the GB system from 2035 to 2050. The framework will cover both normal operating conditions and rare, high impact events, using methods that keep the number of scenarios manageable.

 These scenarios will form the basis for new transmission planning models that properly account for uncertainty and the timing of investment decisions. The post holder will apply optimisation approaches suited to different types of uncertainty, such as stochastic and robust optimisation, to identify investment plans that stay flexible and can adapt as new information comes in, rather than fixing a single plan too early. To ensure these methods work on real, large-scale networks, the post holder will also develop ways to simplify the models so they remain solvable without losing accuracy.

 The role therefore calls for a blend of experience and skills: knowledge of power systems plus the ability to characterise and model uncertainty using statistical and probabilistic techniques, alongside the ability to formulate and solve optimisation problems that incorporate that uncertainty. Experience with methods such as copulas, Bayesian networks or scenario generation is valuable for the first, while experience with stochastic, robust or distributionally robust optimisation is valuable for the second.

 The postholder will join the research team at the University of Strathclyde, led by Professor Keith Bell, holder of the ScottishPower Chair in Future Power Systems. The group is well established, with several related research projects ongoing at PhD and postdoctoral level. The postholder will work closely with Dr Waqquas Bukhsh and Prof Bell within the group, supporting and learning from this wider research effort, so the ability to work well as part of a team is highly valued. The successful candidate will also work closely with NextNet’s industry partners and the project's advisory board, with the research directly informing related studies on system operability and stability. This is a strong opportunity to help shape how uncertainty is built into GB transmission network planning, with a clear path towards use in industry. 

 Initial interviews have been scheduled for week commencing 14 th December 2026.

 For informal enquiries, please contact Keith Bell (Professor) at  keith.bell@strath.ac.uk

We are looking for an experienced researcher to work on Place Based Impact Acceleration Account project Park Royal Net Zero Food Supply Chains. The project is funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) andis based at the Park Royal Industrial area. The aim is to work closely with the food and drink businesses in the area to develop and implement strategies to address the challenges they face with energy, waste, and productivity to reduce carbon cost, improve resilience and drive economic growth.

The appointee will work alongside business development managers and academics to engage with food businesses at Park Royal, to first understand and quantify the energy demand, greenhouse gas emissions and waste from their operations and then investigate and propose solutions that will lead to reductions towards the net zero target.

The successful applicant is expected to have at least a 2.1 Beng/Meng degree in Mechanical, Chemical or other relevant engineering discipline and or other equivalent qualification. The appointee will also be expected to have excellent oral and written communication skills and be able to work closely with other researchers in the group and project collaborators.

About the role

The Bath Mental Health Research Group (MHRG) at the University of Bath undertakes applied research to improve the mental health and wellbeing of children and young people aged 12-25 in the local region. The group is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR).

This Research Associate post sits within MHRG Work Package 3 and focuses on online drug supply and its potential consequences for young people. It will investigate how drugs are promoted, advertised and made accessible through public-facing social-media platforms and associated online channels.

The post builds upon research into emerging drug risks for young people, including our finding that synthetic cannabinoids ('Spice') were detected in approximately one in six vapes seized in English schools (Cozier et al., 2025, Addiction). The new focus is complementary: understanding the online environments in which drug products are offered and discussed.

The postholder will develop and apply reproducible methods for identifying, sampling and coding relevant online content; analyse account relationships, market structure and patterns of advertised supply; and evaluate changes over time. Methods may include computational and social-network analysis, structured content analysis, data visualisation and mixed-method interpretation.

The research will distinguish observed online activity from unverified claims of supply, transactions or exposure. It will produce robust evidence to inform youth-focused harm reduction, prevention and relevant policy, while complying with research ethics, data protection and safeguarding requirements.

About you 

The applicant should have experience with computational analysis and data engineering.

The role will be line-managed and supervised by Professor Christopher Pudney, with Professor Tom Freeman acting as co-supervisor and MHRG Work Package 3 lead. The researcher will work with colleagues across the MHRG and its partners at the Universities of Bristol and Exeter, with opportunities for research skills training and professional development.

We are seeking a motivated and technically skilled researcher with a strong background in computational research, data science or a closely related field. The successful candidate will be able to develop and apply computational methods to investigate complex online systems, with a particular focus on drug supply and potential harms affecting young people.

Essential qualifications, skills and experience:
A PhD in a relevant discipline, such as computer science, data science, mathematics or computational social science, or equivalent professional qualifications and research experience.
Strong practical programming skills, particularly in Python, with experience developing reproducible computational research workflows.
Experience collecting, processing, managing and analysing large or complex datasets, including data engineering and statistical analysis.
Ability to develop, implement and critically evaluate computational methods, working independently to solve research problems.
Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical findings to academic and non-specialist audiences.
Commitment to rigorous, ethical and reproducible research, including appropriate data protection practices.
Desirable experience:
Network or graph analysis, computational modelling, simulation or algorithm development.
Software development, working with APIs, automated data collection or other approaches to investigating online systems.
Research involving social-media platforms, digital marketplaces, online behaviours or independent evaluation of digital services.
Research relating to substance use, illicit markets, public health or young people's wellbeing.

We welcome applicants from different disciplinary backgrounds who can demonstrate the required computational expertise. Previous experience researching drug markets is not essential.

Further information

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE), fixed-term appointment. The post is based at the University of Bath, with regular in-person participation in research activities and project meetings.

We welcome applications from candidates with lived experience (personal or within their family) relevant to the MHRG remit, including mental health difficulties, substance use or neurodiversity. We aim to make this an inclusive recruitment process, with online interviews and interview questions provided in advance.

For an informal discussion, please contact Professor Christopher Pudney (bs1cp@bath.ac.uk) or Professor Tom Freeman (tpf24@bath.ac.uk). Campus visits can be arranged with sufficient notice.

As a member of Research Staff at the University of Bath, you will be encouraged to take up a minimum of 10 days professional development pro rata per year"

We have an excellent international reputation with staff from over 60 different nations and have made a positive commitment towards gender equity and intersectionality receiving a Silver Athena SWAN award. We truly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds will lead to a better environment for our employees and students and encourage applications from all genders, backgrounds, and communities, particularly from under-represented groups, and value the positive impact that will have on the university. We are committed to maintaining a safe and secure environment for our students, staff, and community by reinforcing our Safer Recruitment commitment.

We're very proud to be a signatory of the Armed Forces Covenant. an accredited Disability Confident Leader; autism friendly university, committed to building disability confidence and supporting disabled staff.

Research Associate in Structural Biology
Requisition ID:  29929

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term

Posted Date:  17 Nov 2026

Salary:  £37,369 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 1 December 2026 

 

The Role

 

We are looking for a highly motivated Research Associate to study assembly of multi-subunit RNA polymerases and transertion. The project will be based in Centre for Bacterial Cell Biology of Newcastle University.

 

The successful applicant will have expertise in crystallography and cryo-EM pipelines from sample optimisation to generation of molecular model and structure solution, and experience in purification and assembly of multi-subunit RNA polymerases and membrane proteins.  

 

The role of the Research Associate will be to assemble (in vivo and in vitro) and determine the structures of various complexes of multi-subunit RNA polymerases using crystallography and cryo-EM/ET analyses.

 

This 3 year project is set to start on November 1, 2026.

 

For informal inquiries please contact Prof Nikolay Zenkin. During application, please submit your CV highlighting the experience in expertise essential for the project.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Newcastle University is committed to the responsible use of research metrics as part of our research culture and research strategy. We advocate for the transparent, appropriate, and inclusive use of metrics, guided by expert judgment, to support high-quality, impactful research that is open, collaborative and sustainable. Click here for our full policy statement on the Responsible use of Research Metrics. Click here for a self-study e-learning module on the Responsible Use of Research Metrics.

 

Duration of post is 01/11/2026 – 31/10/2029

 

Key Accountabilities

Analyse various multi-subunit and multi-component complexes using cryo-EM/ET (including: mutagenesis, purification and in vitro assembly of multi-component complexes; samples and grids optimisation; vitrification; screening and collection using Krios, Glacios and Tundra microscopes; solving structures using cryo-EM and XRC software packages)
Provide guidance, where necessary, to other staff and students, including possible supervision of PhD, Master and undergraduate project students as agreed with supervisor.
Contribute to running of the laboratory as agreed with supervisor.
Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes.
Co-ordinate own work with that of others, use problem solving to affect the achievement of research objectives and contribute to the planning of the project(s).
Present information on research progress and outcomes to a Principal Investigator or groups overseeing the research project.
Write up results from own research activity and provide input into the research project’s dissemination, in whatever form (report, papers, chapters, books).
Use research resources (including, where required, laboratories, workshops and specialist equipment) as appropriate.
Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project.
Determine appropriate methodologies for research.
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations.
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications.
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline.
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding.

 

The Person

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

 

Research Associate

Knowledge and Experience in crystallography and cryo-EM pipelines: optimisation of samples, crystallisation conditions and grids; vitrification; screening and collection using Krios, Glacios and Tundra microscopes; solving structures using cryo-EM and XRC software packages
Experience in mutagenesis, purification and in vitro assembly of multi-subunit RNA polymerases and their complexes, membrane proteins, and their analysis using biophysical methods    
Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy
Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences
Proven ability to analyse data and write-up results
Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues
Excellent IT skills in all major office applications
The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems.
Awareness of the research environment
High level of analytical and problem solving capacity
Ability to communicate complex information with clarity
Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team
Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines
Commitment to continued professional development
Understanding of good practice in equality, inclusion and diversity

 

Qualifications

PhD in structural biology

postings.advert_text:
Applications are invited for a Research Associate in Storylistening to work on the EU Horizon project 'Narrative Threads: Co-authoring strategic change with manufacturing SMEs through cluster-mediated Social Science and Humanities-industry knowledge exchange'. The successful candidate will work closely with Professor Sarah Dillon in the Faculty of English, alongside European project partners in academia and industry.

Every year, thousands of European manufacturing SMEs invest in strategic change. They adopt new production technologies, reposition for new markets, respond to sustainability regulations, prepare ownership transitions, or integrate new customer requirements. The technical and financial planning receives structured support through cluster coaching, and technology advisory and skills programmes. But then transition stalls in a pattern so consistent it constitutes a structural condition. Technology is installed yet workers revert to manual processes. The new market strategy is approved yet shop-floor teams cannot explain to customers what changed. The regulatory certification is obtained yet the production culture treats compliance as an external imposition. Management describes the situation as resistance. Workers describe it as a loss of professional standing. Both descriptions are accurate. Neither addresses the mechanism that connects them: narrative friction - that is, the collision between the narratives different organisational actors hold about the same strategic reality.

The postholder will work with experts in socio-technical transformation theory, organisational narrative theory and adult learning and arts-base facilitation theory to design and enable delivery of a method and toolkit to diagnose and address narrative friction in European SMEs. The postholder's primary contribution will be in integrating storylistening effectively into this toolkit. They will contribute to academic publications, conference presentations, policy briefs, and gain industry understanding through ongoing collaboration and immersion.

Applicants should have strong familiarity with the storylistening framework and a Ph.D. in any Humanities or Social Sciences discipline with evidence of a primary engagement with narrative. They should be innovative and dynamic thinkers, adept at interdisciplinary working and with the ability to turn academic frameworks into practical tools. They should be keen to gain experience of working in cross-sector teams and to develop the flexibilities needed to feed academic expertise into industry environments, working together toward shared real-world goals. Applicants should have excellent collaborative, communication and organisational skills, be highly motivated, and thrive in interdisciplinary and cross-sector teams.

The post is 0.62 FTE and available from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The role will be fixed term for 28 months, due to limited funding.

In order for your application to be considered, please upload the following:

Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Cover letter
A sample of your writing that demonstrates as closely as possible your fit with the role responsibilities and person criteria. This can be single-authored or collaborative work, academic writing or for a different sector audience. No more than 6,000 words.
Names and contact details of two referees who are familiar with your work

Informal enquiries about the role are welcomed and should be directed to Professor Sarah Dillon at sjd27@cam.ac.uk. If you have any queries regarding the application process, please contact the School's HR team at sahhr@admin.cam.ac.uk.

The closing date for applications is midnight (GMT) on Monday 14 December 2026. Interviews are planned for the week commencing 4 January 2027, subject to change.

About the Role

We invite applications for one Gillmore Centre for Financial Technology Research Fellow (Post Doc) position at Warwick Business School. This is an opportunity to join one of the largest and most active research centres on financial technology in the UK. The primary mission of the Gilmore Centre is to conduct world-class, cutting-edge research at the intersection of finance and technology, and to create impact from research.

 

The Gillmore Centre for Financial Technology organizes several academic and industry conferences, workshops, and seminars throughout the year. Successful applicants will be able to join these activities and engage with leading researchers and practitioners at the Centre and internationally.

 

If you would like to discuss the position, please do feel free to contact GillmoreLab@wbs.ac.uk.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We invite applicants with strong technical skills, expertise in AI, and interest in academic research. Applicants should hold (or be about to complete) a PhD or strong master’s degree in Computer Science, Business Analytics, FinTech, Statistics, or a related discipline. 

 

Strong quantitative and programming skills, fluency in English, and excellent communication and presentation skills are essential. Candidates with expertise in generative AI, AI agents, reinforcement learning, or VR technology are particularly welcome to apply.

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£36,320 per annum). 

About the Department

The primary mission of the Gilmore Centre is to conduct world-class, cutting-edge research at the intersection of finance and technology. The Centre engages in research exploring the transformative impact of emerging technologies like AI, ML, blockchain, mobile payments, cryptocurrencies and crowdfunding platforms on financial activities.

 

The broad research directions of interest are the following:

 

Societal Impacts and Policy: crypto-currencies, cyber security, financial and privacy regulation, inequality and underserved markets.

Firm and Industry Analysis: blockchain and financial intermediation, smart contracts, nature and source of competition in the financial sector, emerging industry structure, impact of social media on financial markets.

Consumer Analysis: Innovative technology-infused products and services, financial literacy and empowering consumers.

Technology Management: financial principles and instruments to manage data and technology resources such as bandwidth and cloud computing.

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date and time stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. Job Title                                           	Research Fellow 
Job Reference	3832 
Application Closing Date	03/12/2026 
Division, Department	Research Division ,Research Centre for Future Transport and Cities (FTC) 
Salary	Competitive starting salary range from £38,784 up to £42, 254 per annum (dependent upon experience) with the potential to progress. A discretionary range for candidates with exceptional experience can be discussed/considered.
Mode	Fixed Term Until 31/03/2028 , Full Time 

 

Our Mission

 

Coventry University is a global Education Group that empowers students and communities to transform their lives and society through teaching, learning, research, and enterprise.

An ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally.

 

Coventry University's Centre for Future Transport and Cities (CFTC) is a multidisciplinary research centre developing safer, cleaner, smarter, and more accessible transport and urban-mobility solutions. It brings together expertise in connected and autonomous vehicles, transport safety, sustainable mobility, intelligent infrastructure, and future cities, working with academic, industry, and government partners to translate research into practical applications.

 

Access to advanced testing infrastructure is enabled through the Centre for Connected and Autonomous Automotive Research (CCAAR), a collaboration between Coventry University and HORIBA MIRA based at MIRA Technology Park. Through CCAAR, CFTC researchers can develop and validate automated-vehicle technologies using facilities including the Assured CAV Highway and two StreetDrone automated-vehicle platforms.

 

 

The Role

 

As Research Fellow within the Centre for Future Transport and Cities  you will undertake and play a lead role in the development of impactful research and consultancy activity.  Developing and identifying new research objectives, proposals, and impact activities for your own or joint research, while contributing to REF impact rated nationally/internationally excellent.

 

You will apply innovative research methods and extend the research portfolio including the publication of your research results and outcomes. Building internal and external networks for the exchange of information and future collaboration, sharing information, and identifying potential sources of funds will play a key part of this role.

 

Contributing to teaching, learning and development programmes as appropriate, you will use research findings to inform curriculum development while assisting in the development of student research skills.

 

You will specifically be responsible for:

Defining test scenarios and the Operational Design Domain (ODD) for the 5D RAPID demonstrator in collaboration with project partners.
Conducting simulations using IPG CarMaker or CARLA and performing vehicle-in-the-loop tests at MIRA's Assured CAV Highway facility to define, measure, and evaluate relevant project KPIs.
Generating curated datasets, scenario libraries, and workflows to correlate simulation results with proving-ground tests using StreetDrone automated-vehicle platforms and MIRA's Assured CAV Highway facility.

 

Conducting a comprehensive Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) to identify cybersecurity threats arising from the integration of Oxford RF 270° radar sensors into the reference vehicle architecture, assess their potential impact, and derive cybersecurity requirements aligned with emerging BSI and ISO guidance on safety and cybersecurity.

 

The role will allow you to contribute to the 5D RAPID (5D RADAR PERCEPTION FOR INTELLIGENT DRIVING) project that aims to validate an advanced, high-resolution, multi-focal ADS sensing architecture for fast, accurate, and reliable measurement of dynamic objects, thereby addressing critical corner cases in current autonomous driving systems.

 

Qualifications Required

 

PhD (or equivalent) or professional experience equivalent to a PhD demonstrating an ability to carry-out independent research with a 1st Class/2.1 Degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent. 

Our Successful Candidate

 

A highly motivated and experienced Research Fellow with demonstrable expert knowledge and understanding of Automotive Cyber Security, including experience contributing to the innovation and development of the field.  An Advanced knowledge of research methods and techniques with demonstratable adherence to all regulations, you will have the ability to develop research objectives, projects, and proposals for own and joint research.

 

Research sufficient to write up research and produce excellent, high-quality publications in high profile peer reviewed journals and present at national/international events, you will be committed to working collaboratively on research development, delivery and dissemination including interdisciplinary or cross-disciplinary research, public engagement, and knowledge exchange.

 

Within the Centre, the successful applicant will be expected to lead Coventry University's contribution to the 5D RAPID project, coordinate associated activities, and ensure the timely completion and submission of all planned deliverables. The successful applicant will work closely with Prof. Soufiene Djahel, Dr Hesamaldin Jadidbonab, and Kevin Vincent to achieve the project's technical and strategic objectives.

 

For informal enquiries about the position, please contact Prof. Soufiene Djahel at soufiene.djahel@coventry.ac.uk

 

The Benefits

 

As a staff member of Coventry University, you will have access to a wide range of industry leading rewards and benefits which includes:

Excellent Employers Pension Contribution
30 days Annual leave plus Bank Holidays
New Holiday Purchase Scheme up to 5 additional days
Life Assurance 4x Salary
BUPA Cash Plan
50% off Tuition Fees for staff dependants
CU Reward Scheme – Discounts across a range of High Street/ Online Retailers
Cycle To Work scheme

 

Our Culture

 

As a global Education Group, equality, diversity, and inclusion are embedded within the fabric of our organisation and are a key focus of our core values. We harness the power and potential of the diverse cultures, backgrounds, abilities, and experiences of our students, colleagues, and partners to create opportunities for all.

 The Opportunity: 

 Help build the tools that will shape tomorrow’s fault-tolerant quantum computers.

 Research staff at Edinburgh work at the forefront of their fields. As a Research Assistant, you will turn research ideas into reliable, well-engineered software that other people can use and build on.

 We are looking for a Research Assistant to join the Quantum Software Lab for one day per week. You will develop specialised software for the design and analysis of quantum error correction (QEC) schemes.

 The project is a collaboration between the Quantum Software Lab and an industrial partner. Its aim is to create tools for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures: working out how many qubits, how much time and what level of hardware performance are needed to run useful quantum algorithms reliably. The software will be used by researchers at the University and by our partner, so good design, testing and documentation are as important as the underlying science.

 Your main responsibilities will include: 

 Designing, writing and maintaining software for building and analysing quantum error correcting codes and fault-tolerant protocols.

 Developing tools that estimate the physical resources needed to run quantum algorithms on different hardware architectures.

 Writing performance-critical code in Python and C++ and making it available through clear, well-documented Python interfaces.

 Running and automating simulations, such as decoding and logical error rate studies, and checking results against published data.

 Following good software practice, including version control, automated testing, code review and documentation.

 Working with researchers in the Lab and with our industrial partner to agree requirements, report progress and share results.

 What we are looking for: 

 A degree in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics or a related field.

 Knowledge of quantum computing.

 Knowledge of quantum error correction and the design of fault-tolerant systems.

 Strong programming skills in Python and C++.

 Experience of working in software development, for example in industry, research or open-source projects.

 It would also be helpful if you have: 

 Experience with QEC software tools such as Stim, PyMatching or ldpc.

 Experience of packaging and releasing software, or of maintaining code that other people rely on.

 Experience of working with industrial or other external partners.

 This role would suit someone who enjoys combining research and engineering, and who can work independently on their project day while keeping in regular contact with the wider team.

 Join us and you will be part of a friendly, collaborative team doing research with real impact. You will work alongside experts in quantum computing and see your software used to guide the design of future quantum hardware.

 A career with us has a range of other benefits that can be tailored to your lifestyle: 

 Flexible and hybrid working options.

 Generous annual leave, pro rata for part-time staff.

 Training and professional development opportunities.

 Family-friendly policies and staff wellbeing support.

 This post is part time (9 hours per week, equivalent to one day per week). We are happy to discuss how these hours are worked. We are also open to considering requests for hybrid working (on a non-contractual basis) that combines a mix of remote and regular on-campus working.

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 1 December 2026 

 

The Role

 

We are looking for a highly motivated Research Associate to study inhibition of multi-subunit RNA polymerases with natural compounds. The project will be based in Centre for Bacterial Cell Biology of Newcastle University.

 

The successful applicant will have expertise in purification and characterisation of natural antibiotics produced by Actinomycetes, and analysis of their action against RNA polymerases from different bacteria in vivo and in vitro.  

This 2 year project is set to start on November 1, 2026.

 

For informal inquiries please contact Prof Nikolay Zenkin. During application, please submit your CV highlighting the experience in expertise essential for the project.

 

The role of the Research Associate will be to purify natural compounds produced by Actinomycetes, analyse them biophysically and structurally and investigate their modes of action against bacterial RNA polymerases.

Newcastle University is committed to the responsible use of research metrics as part of our research culture and research strategy. Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes.

Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project.
Determine appropriate methodologies for research.
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations.
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications.
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline.
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding.

 

The Person

Knowledge and Experience in optimisation of natural antibiotics production by Actynomycetes, their overproduction in bioreactor, purification to homogenity and characterisation using LC-MS and crystallisation
Experience in purification and in vitro analysis of RNA polymerases from various bacteria
Track record of analysis of modes of action of inhibitors of bacterial transcription in vitro

Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications

PhD in biochemistry or related discipline

About the Role

The Photochemistry for Materials lab is looking for a Research Assistant to join our research team at the University of Warwick under the supervision of Dr Hannes Houck. This position is part-funded through the EPSRC Impact Acceleration Account (IAA) and The Royal Society URF.

 

As global dependence on synthetic materials is intensifying, waste-accumulation of end-of-life products has become a major concern. Specifically fast-growing photopolymer technologies that transform a liquid formulation into a permanently hardened crosslinked photo-polymer are problematic as the resulting thermosetting materials can no longer be recycled. Current photochemical processes that underpin light-based curing processes, however, are single-use and fail to address the urgently needed closed loop recycling of the resulting photopolymer materials. The overall ambition is to make fundamental step-changes in photopolymerisation technology so to effectively and completely re-use initial formulations in a closed-loop process. 

 

You will join our team’s efforts to further develop new photochemistry platforms to scalable and industrially relevant applications of photopolymers with embedded circularity.

 

Applications are invited to join our investigations on two short-term projects. We are looking for a Research Assistant with specific expertise to undertake the following projects:

 

Development of degradable and recyclable materials for photo-3D-printing (EPSRC IAA project Jan-Mar 2027)
Innovative Thermoreversible Photocycloaddition Reactions for Sustainable Materials Design (URF Apr-Jun 2027)

 

More project details are available upon request.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here). 

About You

We are looking to recruit a highly motivated researcher with creative ideas and a passion for science, with knowledge, skills and experience in organic photochemistry in a polymer context, light-based 3D printing techniques, and material characterisation of crosslinked polymer networks.

 

The project involves several challenging research aspects and provides an opportunity to use and share your research skills and experience across team members yet also allows you to train and develop new skills in photochemistry and polymer science.

 

You should be able to work both independently and with other team members. You are expected to have excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including to present your work to peers and/or potential stakeholders at internal and external meetings. You will have the opportunity to engage with the wider research community and departmental activities, including the Warwick Polymer Group and during outreach events or teaching activities.

 

You should have a good honours degree in Chemistry and ideally be near completion of a PhD or equivalent in a relevant scientific discipline (e.g. chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or other science).

About the Department

The Department of Chemistry at Warwick is a thriving and inclusive community of students, academics, researchers, and professional services staff.

 

Our fundamental research pushes boundaries across all major fields of chemistry, while our applied work - delivered through close partnership with the wider scientific community and industry - addresses major global challenges, breakthroughs in health, solar energy harvesting, and sustainable materials.

 

We are proudly outward-facing, and our community is recognised as one of the strongest in the UK. Our extensive national and international relationships create an outstanding environment for collaboration, innovation, and career development. From polymers and catalysts to computation, advanced instrumentation and cutting-edge materials, our research sits at the forefront of the discipline.

 

We are highly interdisciplinary, having long-standing partnerships with the School of Life Sciences, Warwick Medical School, Physics, Manufacturing, Computer Science, Engineering, and Mathematics.

 

We are committed to fostering a supportive and inclusive working and learning environment in which diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are recognised, respected, and valued. Our Athena Swan Silver Award reflects our ongoing efforts to embed equality, diversity, and inclusion into our culture, practices, teaching, and research, and our commitment to supporting the career progression of all staff.

 

Explore our webpages to learn more about the Department of Chemistry’s research and teaching, industry-leading facilities, and the impact of our work.

1) Your CV (max. 3 pages) setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure your CV includes your most up to date qualifications and a summary of your education to date.

3) The names of two academic referees that may be contacted during the application process.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.   

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

The role

We are recruiting a Research Associate / Senior Research Associate in Swarm Construction to design, build and demonstrate robot swarms for timber construction.

You will join SWIFT-BUILD (Swarm-based Inverted Fabrication for Timber Buildings), a €4M EIC project developing robotics and AI for inverted structural assembly. In SWIFT-BUILD, ground-based robots assemble timber structures from the top down, lifting the growing structure to keep construction near ground level. An international consortium brings together architecture, engineering, robotics and responsible innovation, aiming to demonstrate a multi-storey timber pavilion and large-span structural modules.

Your role will contribute to the design of heterogeneous swarm for construction, with a focus on developing modular mobile robots and distributed coordination algorithms for transporting, aligning and assembling timber components and lifting structures. You will integrate hardware and software, and evaluate the resulting systems through real-robot experiments, working with partners on fixing, inspection and stability control.

You will join the Hauert Lab, which engineers swarms across scales and applications, including for environmental monitoring, logistics, and construction. Our supportive, multidisciplinary community offers regular one-to-one meetings, weekly swarm lunches, training, teaching and outreach opportunities. Based at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory, you will have access to workshops, technical support and the Testbed for Industrial Swarm Logistics.

What will you be doing?

Develop swarm coordination algorithms and modular robot hardware for transporting, assembling and lifting timber structures.
Test hardware and algorithms on real robots using DOTS, contributing to SWIFT-BUILD’s timber construction demonstrators.
Work with a multidisciplinary team and stakeholders.
Prepare conference and journal papers for publication.
Contribute to regular events hosted by the hub.

You are working towards or have a relevant PhD degree or equivalent professional qualification/experience in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Maths or closely related discipline (e.g. architecture).
Expertise in swarm robotics or multi-robot systems, algorithm design, robot hardware design and real-robot experimentation.
Demonstrated expertise publishing results in journals and/or conferences.
Experience working in collaborative environments.

The role

We are seeking a motivated, talented and committed individual to join our team as a Research Technician. This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of a novel haematopoietic stem cell (HSC)-based gene therapy for ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), a rare genetic disorder associated with progressive neurodegeneration.

The successful candidate will join the Kemp Lab, based within the School of Psychology and Neuroscience. Our team is dedicated to developing next-generation stem cell and gene therapies for people with neurodegenerative diseases, bringing together expertise in stem cell biology, genetic engineering, and neuroscience.

Working as part of our collaborative and multidisciplinary research team, the successful candidate will contribute to cutting-edge translational research using advanced induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-based models and blood samples from UK patients with A-T to develop and evaluate our gene therapy approach. This will involve maintaining iPSC cultures in accordance with relevant International Society for Stem Cell Research (ISSCR) guidelines, generating and characterising HSCs and microglia from iPSCs, and applying molecular and cellular techniques to assess gene therapy efficacy and safety. The project aims to investigate whether correcting HSCs can improve neuroimmune function and provide a potential therapeutic strategy for the neurological complications of A-T.

What will you be doing?

The post holder will contribute to experimental design, data generation and analysis, and the day-to-day running of the laboratory, ensuring compliance with relevant health and safety requirements and institutional policies. Over the two years you will:

Maintain multiple iPSC lines in accordance with relevant ISSCR guidelines ensuring culture quality, pluripotency and appropriate documentation.
Differentiate iPSC lines into HSCs and microglia using established protocols, and characterise the resulting cell populations using appropriate molecular and cellular techniques
Perform functional assays to assess microglial phagocytosis, dynamics, morphology and interactions with neurons, using techniques including spinning-disk confocal microscopy.
Prepare reagents, maintain stocks of laboratory materials and consumables. You will source and maintain stocks of laboratory materials and consumables.
Work to ensure a safe working environment. You will ensure compliance with Health and Safety regulations and local policies.
Training others in processes and procedures. You will interact with and provide guidance, support and training to students conducting research studies or projects.

You should apply if

You are enthusiastic about contributing to the development of novel stem cell and gene therapies for people with neurodegenerative disorders.
You have practical experience working with induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), including their culture, maintenance and differentiation, or related IPSC techniques.
You have experience in molecular biology techniques, such as nucleic acid and protein extraction, PCR, western blotting and ELISA.
You have experience in cell imaging and histological techniques, including immunofluorescence staining and microscopy.
You have excellent IT, organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise multiple tasks, work independently and meet deadlines.
You have strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team and communicate effectively.
You are proactive, adaptable and eager to learn new techniques, with the ability to take initiative and contribute to the smooth running of the laboratory.

About the role

The Moore group at the Department of Life Sciences, Imperial College London is looking for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to express prioritised biosynthetic gene clusters in cell-free protein synthesis systems. As part of the Horizon Europe project AIMARIA, you will use E. coli and Streptomyces cell-free systems to express the clusters and detect/characterised their natural products. The postdoc will be working alongside, and mentoring, a PhD student who is developing the cell-free platforms further. You will work with Dr Marko Storch and Dr David Bell at the I-HUB and London Biofoundry, where we perform all high-resolution mass spectrometry and downstream analysis. 

Marine microbes hold a vast but underexploited biosynthetic capacity, and most marine microorganisms remain unexplored. AIMARIA (Accelerating Innovation in Marine AI-powered Bioprospecting) is a four-year Horizon Europe project, coordinated by NTNU in Norway, that combines AI-driven prioritisation with cell-free systems and engineered microbial chassis to give sustainable and scalable access to high-value marine natural products. Relevant work from our group includes a Streptomyces venezuelae cell-free protein synthesis toolkit (ACS Synth. Biol. 2021, https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.0c00581) and a review of cell-free synthetic biology for natural product biosynthesis and discovery (Chem. Soc. Rev. 2025, https://doi.org/10.1039/d4cs01198h).

You will join a diverse, collaborative group working on both basic and applied natural product biosynthesis, alongside postdoctoral colleagues on a parallel project developing new-to-nature natural products in Streptomyces, while the group also has regular visiting researchers from Brazil, South Korea and Europe. We encourage applicants with a strong background in molecular biology, microbiology, natural product biosynthesis, to apply, as training will be provided. The group is supportive of your own career development, whether towards an academic fellowship or an industry-facing route

What you would be doing

Your day-to-day work will centre on three areas. First, DNA engineering: designing and cloning marine biosynthetic gene clusters (for example, by Golden Gate DNA assembly) for expression. Third, preparing and analysing samples for high-resolution mass spectrometry and downstream analysis at the I-HUB and London Biofoundry. You will also contribute to lab meetings, AIMARIA consortium meetings (monthly online, yearly in person), publications and grant writing, and will have opportunities to help supervise undergraduate and master's students.

Desirable

Experience mentoring junior researchers, or working with industry partners or on patent applications.

About us:

Our research programme links the world-renowned King’s College London (KCL) Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience, the KCL Department of Early Life Imaging, global leaders in perinatal brain injury research, and the Evelina London Children’s Hospital Complex Motor Disorders Service (St Thomas’ Hospital), a cutting-edge clinical service offering Deep Brain Stimulation for children with refractory movement disorders.   

Our overall aim is to transform understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of childhood dystonia/dystonic cerebral palsy and to translate this knowledge into clinical practice, to improve outcomes and quality of life for children with these severely disabling movement disorders.

About the role:  

This role will support the delivery of an MRC-funded programme of research using neurophysiological techniques to investigate sensorimotor processing and its development in children with dystonia and dystonic cerebral palsy (DCP), and in neonates at risk of developing DCP due to perinatal brain injury.

The position is funded for 18 months full-time.

The successful candidate will contribute to the running of: 

A prospective study of healthy term infants and infants at risk of developing DCP to assess early development of cortical sensorimotor processing using spectral EEG changes in response to sensory stimuli and movement.
A cross-sectional study in children and young people with dystonia/DCP and typically developing children, to investigate sensorimotor processing and the effect of EEG based-neurofeedback, delivered via a Brain Computer Interface (BCI).

You will record and analyse EEG and EMG data from newborn infants, including those at risk of developing DCP due to perinatal brain injury.

You will work directly with children who have severely disabling movement disorders, as well as healthy volunteers, to record neurophysiological data during performance of sensorimotor tasks and run the BCI-neurofeedback studies, including exploring individuals’ cognitive strategies. 

You will also work within the wider research team to support other aspects of our research programme, including recording data from the basal ganglia in children with implanted DBS.

The post-holder will be accountable to Dr Verity McClelland (Clinical Senior Lecturer and Honorary Consultant in Paediatric Clinical Neurophysiology and MRC Clinician Scientist Fellow) in a friendly, small, but growing team. 

You will work with our key collaborators across King’s Health Partners and externally as required for delivery of the research objectives. 

This role requires working face to face with patients, families and healthy volunteers of all ages and requires working on-site predominantly at Evelina / St Thomas’ hospital campus and also at Denmark Hill campus.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week) and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 18 months or 15/08/28 if this is sooner.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information. 

About you: 

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential criteria 

PhD or equivalent with clinical research experience in a relevant subject *
Skilled in coding using Matlab
Skilled in recording and analysing neurophysiological data (EEG/EMG), including in children and infants
Experience in recruiting and working with patients, particularly children and their families
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Excellent organizational and time-management skills
Ability to work independently and use own initiative
Excellent team-working skills

Desirable criteria

Knowledge of data confidentiality and data protection act
Skilled in statistical analysis and hypothesis testing
Skills in database building and maintenance  
Ability to create and maintain basic websites
Experience in formal childhood developmental assessment

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.[VM1]

The Stoneygate Centre for Empathic Healthcare at the University of Leicester is seeking a Research Assistant to support a mixed-methods study evaluating the feasibility of implementing a newly developed measure of therapeutic empathy, the Rapid Assessment of Therapeutic Empathy (RATE), in an NHS setting.

 
RATE has been developed to capture patients’ overall perceptions of therapeutic empathy in healthcare encounters. This study will explore the feasibility of administering RATE in NHS practice, alongside patients’ experiences of completing the measure and healthcare staff’s experiences of implementing it. The findings will inform the potential wider use of RATE in clinical practice and future research.

 
Working closely with Dr Amber Bennett-Weston and Professor Jeremy Howick, you will support applications for NHS research ethics and Health Research Authority (HRA) approval, coordinate implementation and data collection, and contribute to quantitative and qualitative data analysis. Koch History Centre Senior Fellowship

 University of Oxford - Faculty of History

 About the role  

 The Koch History Centre provides a new institutional home in Oxford for the pursuit of world-class historical research. Funded initially for 5 years, the Centre received its first intake of fellows in 2025. The Centre aims to promote curiosity-driven humanities research with a strong emphasis on multi- and inter-disciplinary approaches to the study of history.  The Centre is administered by the Faculty of History, which is based in the new, purpose-built Schwarzman Centre for the Humanities, Radcliffe Observatory Quarter, Woodstock Road, Oxford OX2 6GG, and is hosted by Wadham College, Parks Rd, Oxford OX1 3PN.

 The Centre will appoint 3 Senior Fellows each year. Senior fellowships will be of one year’s duration and will be open to individuals whose PhD was granted more than 10 years before the application submission deadline (measured from the viva voce examination). Allowances will be made in the assessment of an applicant’s track record for periods of maternity or carer's leave, and illness.

 Please ensure that you have applied to the correct ad for your situation, as ineligible Senior Fellowship applications will not be considered for the Fellowship posts.   

 The theme chosen for 2027-8 is Trust and Credibility . Given the Centre’s commitment to attracting historians with expertise in a broad range of periods and cultures, these terms should be understood as widely as possible. We welcome applications from scholars of ancient history through to contemporary history, and across all geographical and thematic ranges.

 About you  

 You will hold doctorate granted more than 10 years prior to the application submission deadline (measured from the viva voce examination), and have an established international publication record and reputation with a track record of internationally outstanding research. You will also be able to evidence your experience of academic leadership, public engagement/research impact, and expertise in multi- and inter-disciplinary approaches to the study of history. Experience of leading research programmes, including setting the strategic direction would be desirable.

 This post is full time, fixed-term for 12 months.

 Application Process  

 Applications must be submitted through the University's online recruitment portal.

 As part of your application, you will be required to:

 Upload a curriculum vitae of no more than five pages.

 Complete the supporting statement using the  online form , explaining how you meet the selection criteria and answering questions about your proposed research project. Once completed, you will receive a PDF copy by email, which must be uploaded to your application .

 Provide the names and contact details of two referees.

 Please refer to the further particulars for detailed instructions, including document formatting and application requirements these can be found via the 'Apply' button above.

 Please note that applications which do not include the supporting statement generated using the online form, or which exceed the specified limits, will be deemed ineligible.  

 All practical and procedural enquiries should be directed to   recruitments@history.ox.ac.uk . Enquiries will be treated in strict confidence and will not form part of the selection decision.

 You will receive an automated email confirming receipt of your application. Please check your spam or junk folder if you do not receive this. Further correspondence may also be sent through the recruitment portal.

 Due to the volume of applications received, we are unable to provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants.

 Location: Old Road Campus Research Building, Roosevelt Drive, Headington, Oxford, OX3 7DQ

 We are seeking to appoint a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join the research group of Professor David Withers in the Oxford Centre for Immuno-Oncology in the Nuffield Department of Medicine. Professor Withers leads the Tumour-Immune cell Dynamics Lab, which investigates the regulation of adaptive immune responses in cancer, utilising in vivo models to discern new mechanistic insight into cellular behaviour, fate and function.

 The postdoctoral research position is part of a Cancer Research UK Discovery Research Programme, focused on deciphering tissue-specific mechanisms that impede the anti-tumour T cell response in colorectal cancer. The majority of colorectal cancer patients are currently left without any effective treatments for late-stage disease where metastases, particularly to the liver present a particular challenge. How liver metastases mediate both local and systemic suppression of anti-tumour immunity in the face of clinically approved immunotherapies remains incompletely understood and multiple mechanisms featuring an array of cell types have been proposed.

 You will manage your own academic research and administrative activities. This involves small scale project management, to co-ordinate multiple aspects of work to meet deadlines. You will adapt existing and develop new scientific techniques and experimental protocols. You will be responsible for testing hypotheses and analysing scientific data from a variety of sources, reviewing and refining working hypotheses as appropriate. As a Postdoctoral Researcher you will represent the lab by presenting your research findings at national and international symposia.

 It is essential that you hold, or are close to completing, a PhD/DPhil in Immunology or Biomedical Sciences, with a strong interest in cancer. You should hold a Home Office Personal Licence, have substantial experience in multi-parameter flow cytometry, spatial analyses, in vivo models of immune responses and bioinformatic analysis, including bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing. Excellent communication skills, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and experience supporting and training junior researchers are also required. Experience with in vivo cancer models, analysing T cell phenotype and function or genetically engineered mouse models would be advantageous.

 Applications for this vacancy should be made online, and you will need to upload a supporting statement and CV. Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Please restrict your documentation to your CV and supporting statement only. Any other documents will be requested at a later date.

 Informal enquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor David Withers ( david.withers@immonc.ox.ac.uk ). The post is ideal for someone a strong interest and background in in vivo experimentation.

 This position is offered full time on a fixed term contract until 31 December 2029 and is funded by Cancer Research UK.

 Only applications received before 12 midday on 11 December 2026 will be considered. Please quote 189651 on all correspondence.

 We are seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Researcher to join Professor David Withers’ Tumour-Immune Cell Dynamics Lab at the Oxford Centre for Immuno-Oncology, Nuffield Department of Medicine. Funded by a Wellcome Discovery Award, the research will investigate the formation and function of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in cancer, focusing on how lymphoid aggregates influence immune cell behaviour and function within different tumours. The project will utilise established in vivo cancer models, genetically engineered mouse models and advanced immunological techniques to better understand the regulation of anti-tumour immune responses.

Excellent communication skills, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and experience supporting and training junior researchers are also required. Experience with in vivo cancer models, analysing T cell phenotype and function or genetically engineered mouse models would be advantageous.

 Only applications received before 12 midday on 11 December 2026 will be considered. Please quote 189723 on all correspondence.

 Who we are 

 Rated a top three modern University in London, we provide an engaging portfolio of apprenticeships, short courses, undergraduate and postgraduate degrees. We also have an excellent research profile and were jointly recognised as the best modern university in the country for research, and the highest-ranked modern university in London in REF2021.

 The Role 

 We are recruiting to the role of Research Assistant to join Dr Simon Dyall's expanding team. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a project investigating how dietary intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids influences brain development of extremely preterm infants. The project is supported by the Waterloo Foundation.   

 Key responsibilities will include:

 Maintaining accurate records, including participant files, regulatory documentation, and data entry in study databases.

 Supporting the development of publications and educational materials based on study findings.

 Attending regular team meetings and contributing to project planning and progress reports.   

 The successful candidate will have skills and experience in:

 Clinical or nutrition research, including data collection and dietary assessment methods.

 Data management and analysis experience.

 Strong organizational and interpersonal skills and excellent attention to detail. 

 If you have any specific questions on the role, please contact Dr Simon Dyall,  simon.dyall@roehampton.ac.uk .

 The University is committed to promoting diversity and equality of opportunity and aims to create a culture and environment where students and staff are treated fairly. The University is an equal opportunities and ‘disability confident’ employer.

 Staff have access to our highly competitive RoePlus benefits package ranging from sector leading family related leave, discounts at over 200 high street shops and brands, discounted IT hardware and software.

 The closing date for completed applications is: 23 November 2026 

 It is expected that interviews will be held on 08 December 2026 

 You are encouraged to apply promptly, as we reserve the right to close the role and interview before the dates stated above. 

 Visa Sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates who apply for this role must already hold and be able to maintain their legal right to work in the UK.

 An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Senior Research Fellow to work on a NIHR ARC Wessex funded programme within the Integrated Approaches to Health and Social Care (IHSC) theme which is part of the NIHR ARC Wessex.

 This post will support the Integrated Approaches to Health and Social Care (IHS) theme. The senior research fellow will undertake applied research within the flagship programme Dementia Care at Home and support the delivery of agile projects within the wider IHS theme.

 The IHS flagship will develop, test and implement integrated, person-centred models of care that enable people with complex needs to live well at home and within their communities for longer. The flagship will focus on strengthening neighbourhood health and care systems, improving coordination across health, social care, local government and voluntary sectors, and reducing inequalities in access to support, with an initial emphasis on dementia care closer to home.    � Knowledge, experience and understanding of challenges in Social Care, national initiatives in Dementia research, research implementation and work with local authorities would be an important advantage.

 Although role advertised at 0.6 FTE we will consider lower commitment.

Full time or part time (0.4 - 1FTE) and fixed term until August 2028

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of a new MA Architecture programme through a major international academic partnership in the Middle East. Working as part of a high-profile research and curriculum development project, you will investigate global and regional approaches to architecture education, helping to shape an innovative, research-led and practice-based programme that responds to contemporary challenges in culture, climate, governance and innovation.

You will undertake and synthesise research, engage with academic, professional and industry stakeholders, and contribute to curriculum design, programme development and educational strategy. Working closely with senior academics and external partners, you will support the creation of distinctive approaches to teaching, learning and research.

This role offers a unique opportunity to influence the future of architecture education while developing expertise in pedagogical innovation, research and international academic collaboration. We are seeking a highly organised and analytical researcher with excellent communication skills, the ability to manage multiple workstreams, and a passion for shaping new educational opportunities.

Please see Information Pack for further details.

This role is available on a full time or part time basis until August 2028
